claim: The construction of cilia and flagella depends on intraflagellar transport (IFT), the bidirectional movement of two protein complexes (IFT-A and IFT-B) driven by specific kinesin and dynein motors.
source: The construction of cilia and flagella depends on intraflagellar transport (IFT), the bidirectional movement of two protein complexes (IFT-A and IFT-B) driven by specific kinesin and dynein motors.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about IFT and is supported by citations in the introduction section.

claim: IFT-B and kinesin are associated to anterograde transport.
source: IFT-B and kinesin are associated to anterograde transport whereas IFT-A and dynein participate to retrograde transport.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: IFT-A and dynein participate to retrograde transport.
source: IFT-B and kinesin are associated to anterograde transport whereas IFT-A and dynein participate to retrograde transport.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: The small GTPase IFT27, a member of the IFT-B complex, is essential for retrograde cargo transport in Trypanosoma brucei.
source: Surprisingly, the small GTPase IFT27, a member of the IFT-B complex, turns out to be essential for retrograde cargo transport in Trypanosoma brucei.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data showing accumulation of IFT proteins and failure to import IFT-A and dynein.

claim: IFT27 depletion causes failure to import both the IFT-A complex and the IFT dynein into the flagellar compartment.
source: We reveal that this is due to failure to import both the IFT-A complex and the IFT dynein into the flagellar compartment.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data showing IFT140 and DHC1b concentrated at the flagellum base but not inside the flagellum in IFT27 RNAi cells.

claim: The GDP-locked version of IFT27 is unable to enter the flagellum.
source: The GDP-locked version is unable to enter the flagellum and to interact with other IFT-B proteins and its sole expression prevents flagellum formation.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence and live microscopy data showing IFT27T19N localized only in the cytoplasm.

claim: The GDP-locked version of IFT27 is unable to interact with other IFT-B proteins.
source: The GDP-locked version is unable to enter the flagellum and to interact with other IFT-B proteins and its sole expression prevents flagellum formation.
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments showing IFT27T19N fails to bring down IFT172 and IFT22.

claim: Expression of the GDP-locked version of IFT27 alone prevents flagellum formation.
source: The GDP-locked version is unable to enter the flagellum and to interact with other IFT-B proteins and its sole expression prevents flagellum formation.
evidence: This is supported by data showing short flagella in induced IFT27RNAiREST19N cells.

claim: A GTPase-competent IFT27 is required for association to the IFT complex.
source: These findings demonstrate that a GTPase-competent IFT27 is required for association to the IFT complex and that IFT27 plays a role in the cargo loading of the retrograde transport machinery.
evidence: This is inferred from the inability of the GDP-locked version to interact with IFT-B proteins and enter the flagellum.

claim: IFT27 plays a role in the cargo loading of the retrograde transport machinery.
source: These findings demonstrate that a GTPase-competent IFT27 is required for association to the IFT complex and that IFT27 plays a role in the cargo loading of the retrograde transport machinery.
evidence: This is supported by data showing failure of IFT-A and dynein to enter the flagellum in the absence of IFT27.

claim: IFT is an evolutionary conserved process for assembling cilia and flagella.
source: Although cilia and flagella can differ by their functions, they share the same basic structure and are mainly assembled by an evolutionary conserved process called intraflagellar transport (IFT) (Kozminski et al., 1993; Rosenbaum and Witman, 2002).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: During IFT, large protein complexes called IFT trains are moved from the base to the tip of the flagellum by kinesin-2.
source: During IFT, large protein complexes called IFT trains are moved from the base to the tip of the flagellum by kinesin-2 (anterograde IFT) (Kozminski et al., 1995) and back towards the base by cytoplasmic dynein-1b/2 (retrograde IFT) (Pazour et al., 1998).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: IFT trains are moved back towards the base by cytoplasmic dynein-1b/2.
source: During IFT, large protein complexes called IFT trains are moved from the base to the tip of the flagellum by kinesin-2 (anterograde IFT) (Kozminski et al., 1995) and back towards the base by cytoplasmic dynein-1b/2 (retrograde IFT) (Pazour et al., 1998).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The IFT particles are composed of at least 20 different proteins.
source: The IFT particles are composed of at least 20 different proteins (Cole et al., 1998; Follit et al., 2009; Taschner et al., 2011) and can be divided in two different complexes known as complex A (made of at least 6 proteins) and B (made of at least 14 proteins) that are needed for retrograde and anterograde IFT respectively.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: IFT complex A is made of at least 6 proteins.
source: The IFT particles are composed of at least 20 different proteins (Cole et al., 1998; Follit et al., 2009; Taschner et al., 2011) and can be divided in two different complexes known as complex A (made of at least 6 proteins) and B (made of at least 14 proteins) that are needed for retrograde and anterograde IFT respectively.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: IFT complex B is made of at least 14 proteins.
source: The IFT particles are composed of at least 20 different proteins (Cole et al., 1998; Follit et al., 2009; Taschner et al., 2011) and can be divided in two different complexes known as complex A (made of at least 6 proteins) and B (made of at least 14 proteins) that are needed for retrograde and anterograde IFT respectively.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Inactivation of IFT-B proteins or of the kinesin motor results in the failure to construct the flagellum.
source: Inactivation of IFT-B proteins or of the kinesin motor results in the failure to construct the flagellum whereas IFT-A proteins and the IFT dynein contribute to retrograde transport.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: IFT27 exhibits sequence homologies with the family of Rab-like small G proteins.
source: However, two IFT proteins belonging to the IFT complex B do not share those features. Instead, they exhibit sequence homologies with the family of Rab-like small G proteins, which can function to regulate vesicle movement along actin and tubulin networks (Stenmark, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 1 and citation.

claim: IFT22 lacks the G4 domain needed for recognition of the guanine base.
source: Despite being homologous to the Rab-like proteins, IFT22 lacks the G4 domain needed for recognition of the guanine base (Paduch et al., 2001) and GTP binding and hydrolysis has not been demonstrated to date.
evidence: This is supported by citation.

claim: IFT27 possesses all five RAS-GTPase consensus sequences needed for GTPase activity and GDP binding.
source: The second protein is termed IFT27 (or Rab-like 4) and contrary to IFT22, it possesses all five RAS-GTPase consensus sequences needed for GTPase activity and GDP binding.
evidence: This is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 1.

claim: IFT27 is structurally similar to Rab8 and Rab11.
source: Structurally, the protein is similar to Rab8 and Rab11 and is capable of GTP hydrolysis (Bhogaraju et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation.

claim: IFT27 is capable of GTP hydrolysis.
source: Structurally, the protein is similar to Rab8 and Rab11 and is capable of GTP hydrolysis (Bhogaraju et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation.

claim: IFT27 is part of the IFT complex B core.
source: IFT27 is part of the IFT complex B core, where the protein interacts directly with IFT25 (Lucker et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citation and co-immunoprecipitation data in the study.

claim: IFT27 interacts directly with IFT25.
source: IFT27 is part of the IFT complex B core, where the protein interacts directly with IFT25 (Lucker et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citation.

claim: The IFT25/27 sub-complex is associated with the rest of the IFT complex B prior to flagellum entry.
source: This IFT25/27 sub-complex is associated with the rest of the IFT complex B prior to flagellum entry, suggesting a possible regulatory role during the entry of the IFT machinery (Wang et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation.

claim: RNAi-mediated knockdown of IFT27 causes flagellar defects in Chlamydomonas.
source: In Chlamydomonas, RNAi-mediated knockdown of IFT27 causes flagellar defects (Qin et al., 2007), supporting its role during flagellar assembly, although its exact contribution was not investigated.
evidence: This is supported by citation.

claim: The T. brucei IFT27 gene encodes a predicted protein of 183 amino acids with a predicted molecular weight of 20.64 kDa.
source: The T. brucei IFT27 gene (TritrypDB Accession number Tb927.3.5550) has a 552 nucleotide-long sequence that encodes a predicted protein of 183 amino acids (predicted molecular weight of 20.64 kDa).
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis of the gene.

claim: IFT27 shares significant homology with the Rab-like 4 (RABL4) GTPase found in Homo sapiens and vertebrates.
source: BLAST analyses show that IFT27 shares significant homology (E value = 2e−27) with the Rab-like 4 (RABL4) GTPase found in Homo sapiens and vertebrates.
evidence: This is based on BLAST analysis data.

claim: IFT27 homologues are present in the genomes of all ciliated organisms except in Drosophila, C. elegans, Giardia, and some ferns and mosses.
source: IFT27 homologues are present in the genomes of all ciliated organisms except in Drosophila, C. elegans, Giardia, and some ferns and mosses (van Dam et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation.

claim: All IFT27 sequences lack the prenylation motif found in Rab proteins.
source: Additionally, all IFT27 sequences lack the prenylation motif (two cysteins at the C terminal end) found in Rab proteins suggesting that the protein is not lipid modified and thus unlikely to interact with the cellular membrane.
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis shown in Figure 1.

claim: IFT27 is unlikely to interact with the cellular membrane due to lack of prenylation motif.
source: Additionally, all IFT27 sequences lack the prenylation motif (two cysteins at the C terminal end) found in Rab proteins suggesting that the protein is not lipid modified and thus unlikely to interact with the cellular membrane.
evidence: This is inferred from the absence of prenylation motif.

claim: The anti-IFT27 antibody detected a single band migrating at a position close to the predicted size of 20 kDa in wild-type cells.
source: Western blot analyses using the anti-IFT27 antibody showed a single band migrating at a position close to the predicted size of 20 kDa in wild-type cells (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is shown in Western blot data in Figure 2A.

claim: In trypanosomes expressing the GFP::IFT27 fusion, the anti-IFT27 antibody detected an additional band migrating close to the 50 kDa marker.
source: In trypanosomes expressing the GFP::IFT27 fusion, the same antibody detected an additional band migrating close to the 50 kDa marker. This molecular weight is compatible with the expected mass of the fusion protein (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is shown in Western blot data in Figure 2A.

claim: IFT27 localizes all along the flagellum, starting at the base of the organelle and reaching its distal tip.
source: In wild-type cells, the anti-IFT27 antibody produced a signal all along the flagellum, starting at the base of the organelle and reaching its distal tip where it was sometimes brighter (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence data in Figure 2B.

claim: GFP::IFT27 clearly traffics along the flagellum with typical bidirectional IFT.
source: The use of live microscopy demonstrated that the fusion protein clearly traffics along the flagellum (Figure 2C,D; Video 1) where typical bidirectional IFT was visualized.
evidence: This is shown by live microscopy data in Figure 2C,D and Video 1.

claim: The mean anterograde velocity of GFP::IFT27 was 2.5 ± 0.68 µm/s.
source: The mean anterograde velocity was 2.5 ± 0.68 µm/s (n = 234) and mean retrograde velocity was measured at 3.8 ± 1.5 µm/s (n = 269).
evidence: This is based on kymograph analysis of live microscopy data.

claim: The mean retrograde velocity of GFP::IFT27 was 3.8 ± 1.5 µm/s.
source: The mean anterograde velocity was 2.5 ± 0.68 µm/s (n = 234) and mean retrograde velocity was measured at 3.8 ± 1.5 µm/s (n = 269).
evidence: This is based on kymograph analysis of live microscopy data.

claim: IFT27 expression was inhibited after 48 hr of RNAi induction.
source: Western blot analysis using the anti-IFT27 polyclonal antibody showed that the IFT27 expression was inhibited after 48 hr of induction (Figure 4A) and IFT27RNAi cells showed a clear growth defect upon depletion of the protein (Figure 4B), in line with the essential role of the flagellum for the trypanosome cell cycle (Kohl et al., 2003).
evidence: This is shown by Western blot data in Figure 4A.

claim: IFT27RNAi cells showed a clear growth defect upon depletion of the protein.
source: Western blot analysis using the anti-IFT27 polyclonal antibody showed that the IFT27 expression was inhibited after 48 hr of induction (Figure 4A) and IFT27RNAi cells showed a clear growth defect upon depletion of the protein (Figure 4B), in line with the essential role of the flagellum for the trypanosome cell cycle (Kohl et al., 2003).
evidence: This is shown by growth curve data in Figure 4B.

claim: IFT27RNAi cells induced for 72 hr assemble abnormally short flagella with a mean axonemal length of 4.0 ± 6.8 µm.
source: Immunofluorescence assays results revealed that IFT27RNAi cells induced for 72 hr assemble abnormally short flagella (Figure 4C bottom panel, arrowhead) with a mean axonemal length of 4.0 ± 6.8 µm (n = 100) instead of 20.5 ± 2.8 µm (n = 100) for non-induced controls (Figure 4C, top panel).
evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence data in Figure 4C and quantitative measurements.

claim: Non-induced IFT27RNAi control cells have a mean axonemal length of 20.5 ± 2.8 µm.
source: Immunofluorescence assays results revealed that IFT27RNAi cells induced for 72 hr assemble abnormally short flagella (Figure 4C bottom panel, arrowhead) with a mean axonemal length of 4.0 ± 6.8 µm (n = 100) instead of 20.5 ± 2.8 µm (n = 100) for non-induced controls (Figure 4C, top panel).
evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence data in Figure 4C and quantitative measurements.

claim: IFT172 and IFT22 accumulate in the short flagella of induced IFT27RNAi cells.
source: However, unexpected accumulations of IFT172 and IFT22 were found in the short flagella of induced IFT27RNAi cells (Figure 5Ae–h, arrows) and the same results were observed for PIFTC3, a candidate IFT-B protein (Franklin and Ullu, 2010) (unpublished data).
evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence data in Figure 5A.

claim: GFP::IFT52 accumulates inside the short flagella of 72-hr induced IFT27RNAi cells.
source: Whereas in non-induced cells, GFP::IFT52 was localized in the cytoplasm but also concentrated at the base of the flagellum and inside the organelle (Figure 5Ba–d), 72-hr induced cells clearly showed an accumulation of the protein inside their short flagella (Figure 5Be–h).
evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence data in Figure 5B.

claim: At least four members of the IFT-B complex accumulate inside the flagellum of the induced IFT27RNAi cells.
source: Together, these observations demonstrate that at least four members of the IFT-B complex accumulate inside the flagellum of the induced IFT27RNAi cells.
evidence: This is based on immunofluorescence data showing accumulation of IFT172, IFT22, PIFTC3, and IFT52.

claim: Induced IFT27RNAi cells exhibit a significant accumulation of electron-dense material that likely corresponds to excessive IFT material.
source: First, a significant accumulation of electron-dense material that likely corresponds to excessive IFT material was observed (Figure 5Cc–d).
evidence: This is shown by transmission electron microscopy data in Figure 5C.

claim: The axoneme in induced IFT27RNAi cells was frequently disrupted and sometimes even split into two.
source: In addition, the axoneme was frequently disrupted and sometimes even split into two (Figure 5C,D) and an enlarged, often disorganized PFR structure was frequently observed.
evidence: This is shown by transmission electron microscopy data in Figures 5C and 6.

claim: Over 61% of the flagellar sections in induced IFT27RNAi cells displayed the combination of IFT accumulation, axoneme disruption, and enlarged PFR.
source: Over 61% of the flagellar sections (n = 77) displayed the combination of the three phenotypes.
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of TEM sections.

claim: In non-induced IFT27RNAi cells, GFP::DHC1b signal was present around the base of the flagellum and displayed a punctuated staining inside the organelle and in the cytoplasm.
source: In non-induced IFT27RNAi cells, the GFP::DHC1b signal was present around the base of the flagellum and displayed a punctuated staining inside the organelle and in the cytoplasm (Figure 7a–d) confirming previous localization experiments performed with the anti-DHC1b antibody (our unpublished data).
evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence data in Figure 7.

claim: When IFT27RNAi cells were induced for 3 days, DHC1b was not detected inside the short flagella but instead the protein appeared concentrated at the base of the flagellum.
source: When IFT27RNAi cells were induced for 3 days, DHC1b was not detected inside the short flagella but instead the protein appeared concentrated at the base of the flagellum (Figure 7e–h), suggesting defects in flagellum entry.
evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence data in Figure 7.

claim: In non-induced IFT27RNAi cells, TdT::IFT140 is localized inside the flagellum compartment.
source: In non-induced cells, the fusion protein is localized inside the flagellum compartment (Figure 8b) as for the anti-IFT172 (Figure 8c).
evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence data in Figure 8.

claim: In 3-day-induced IFT27RNAi cells, TdT::IFT140 is only found concentrated at the base of the organelle and not inside the flagellar compartment.
source: In 3-day-induced IFT27RNAi cells, TdT::IFT140 is only found concentrated at the base of the organelle and not inside the flagellar compartment (Figure 8f,h).
evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence data in Figure 8.

claim: Both actors of the retrograde transport fail to enter the flagellum in the absence of IFT27.
source: Therefore, both actors of the retrograde transport fail to enter the flagellum in the absence of IFT27, suggesting that this protein, despite being a member of the IFT-B complex, is a major controller of retrograde transport.
evidence: This is based on data showing both IFT140 and DHC1b fail to enter the flagellum in IFT27 RNAi cells.

claim: The RNAi-resistant version of IFT27 complements gene function upon silencing of the endogenous IFT27 gene copies.
source: These results show that the RNAi-resistant version of IFT27 complements gene function upon silencing of the endogenous IFT27 gene copies and demonstrate the specificity of the phenotypes observed in the IFT27RNAi cell line.
evidence: This is shown by growth curves and immunofluorescence data in Figure 9.

claim: The growth rate of the IFT27RNAiRESQ67L cell line did not vary after induction.
source: After induction, the growth rate of the IFT27RNAiRESQ67L cell line did not vary (Figure 11B), while the IFT27RNAiREST19N cells showed impaired growth (Figure 11D).
evidence: This is shown by growth curve data in Figure 11B.

claim: The IFT27RNAiREST19N cells showed impaired growth after induction.
source: After induction, the growth rate of the IFT27RNAiRESQ67L cell line did not vary (Figure 11B), while the IFT27RNAiREST19N cells showed impaired growth (Figure 11D).
evidence: This is shown by growth curve data in Figure 11D.

claim: The modified T19N protein produces a phenotype only when the endogenous IFT27 expression is inhibited, suggesting a recessive effect of the T19N mutation.
source: Therefore, the modified T19N protein produces a phenotype only when the endogenous IFT27 expression is inhibited, suggesting a recessive effect of the T19N mutation.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that growth defects only appear after RNAi induction.

claim: IFT27RNAiREST19N cells build unusually short flagella after 3 days of induction.
source: Immunofluorescence assays using the monoclonal antibodies Mab25 and L8C4 showed that the IFT27RNAiRESQ67L (GTP-locked) cells were undistinguishable from their non-induced control (Figure 11E) whereas IFT27RNAiREST19N (GDP-locked) cells build unusually short flagella after 3 days of induction (Figure 11F, arrows).
evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence data in Figure 11F.

claim: Flagellar length of IFT27RNAiREST19N cells dropped to 3.7 ± 3.1 µm after induction compared to 17.6 ± 2.1 µm for the non-induced controls.
source: The flagellar length of the IFT27RNAiRESQ67L cell line showed no significant differences between non-induced (16.9 ± 1.9 µm, n = 100) and induced cells (16.6 ± 2.98 µm, n = 100) whereas flagellar length of IFT27RNAiREST19N cells dropped to 3.7 ± 3.1 µm (n = 79) after induction compared to 17.6 ± 2.1 µm (n = 100) for the non-induced controls.
evidence: This is based on quantitative measurements of flagellar length.

claim: The expression of a GDP or GTP-locked form of IFT27 has a slightly negative dominant impact on the formation of the trypanosome flagellum.
source: However, by carefully analysing both IFT27RNAiREST19N and IFT27RNAiRESQ67L cells in non-induced conditions, we noticed that the length of the flagellum was shorter by about 3 µm compared to cell that are not expressing a mutated form of IFT27 (Figure 12). This interesting result indicates that the expression of a GDP or GTP-locked form of IFT27 has a slightly negative dominant impact on the formation of the trypanosome flagellum.
evidence: This is shown by flagellar length measurements in Figure 12.

claim: The induced IFT27RNAiREST19N cells did not show signs of IFT B complex accumulation but IFT172 was found concentrated at the base of the organelle.
source: While the IFT172 staining looked normal in the non-induced context (Figure 13Aa–d), the induced IFT27RNAiREST19N cells did not show signs of IFT B complex accumulation but IFT172 was found concentrated at the base of the organelle (Figure 13Ae–h) in a way reminding of the localization of the IFT140 protein in the IFT27RNAi cell line (Figure 7).
evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence data in Figure 13A.

claim: The expression of IFT27RNAiREST19N in the absence of endogenous IFT27 triggers an anterograde IFT phenotype.
source: The phenotype obtained in the induced IFT27RNAiREST19N cells is reminiscent to the ones observed upon disruption of the anterograde IFT machinery (Pazour et al., 2000; Absalon et al., 2008b) and shows that the expression of IFT27RNAiREST19N in the absence of endogenous IFT27 triggers an anterograde IFT phenotype.
evidence: This is inferred from the similarity of the phenotype to known anterograde IFT defects.

claim: DHC1b remained at the flagellum base in induced cells solely expressing the T19N mutant protein.
source: In contrast, DHC1b remained at the flagellum base in induced cells solely expressing the T19N mutant protein (Figure 14e–h, arrow).
evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence data in Figure 14.

claim: The GDP-locked version does not sustain the entry of the IFT-B complex in the flagellar compartment, leading to an anterograde phenotype.
source: In conclusion, the GDP-locked version does not sustain the entry of the IFT-B complex in the flagellar compartment, leading to an anterograde phenotype. Nevertheless, dynein is still targeted to the base of the flagellum.
evidence: This is inferred from the localization data of IFT172 and DHC1b in cells expressing the T19N mutant.

claim: IFT27RNAiRESQ67L is localized inside the flagellum in non-induced and induced cells.
source: Immunofluorescence assays using the anti-IFT27 and the anti-GFP antibodies (Figure 15) showed that IFT27RNAiRESQ67L is localized inside the flagellum in non-induced (Figure 15Aa–d) and induced (Figure 15Ae–h) cells as the unmodified IFT27RNAiRES::YFP protein (Figure 3).
evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence data in Figure 15A.

claim: The fluorescent Q67L modified protein traffics inside the flagellum in both non-induced and induced conditions.
source: In addition, the fluorescent Q67L modified protein traffics inside the flagellum in both conditions (Figure 15B; Video 3) and kymograph analyses demonstrated anterograde and retrograde train speed similar to the unmodified protein (Figure 15B, Figure 3).
evidence: This is shown by live microscopy and kymograph data in Figure 15B and Video 3.

claim: The IFT27RNAiREST19N::YFP fusion protein was always found in the cytoplasm in both non-induced and induced situations.
source: Strikingly, the IFT27RNAiREST19N::YFP fusion protein was always found in the cytoplasm in both non-induced and induced situations (Figure 15C).
evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence data in Figure 15C.

claim: No signal of IFT27RNAiREST19N::YFP could be detected in the flagellum by immunofluorescence assays or by live cell imaging.
source: No signal could be detected in the flagellum, neither by immunofluorescence assays (Figure 15C) nor by live cell imaging (Video 4) in both non-induced and induced cells, suggesting that the modified protein is not able to access the flagellum.
evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence data in Figure 15C and Video 4.

claim: The immune complexes formed by IFT27RNAiRES::YFP and IFT27RNAiRESQ67L::YFP contain both IFT22 and IFT172.
source: Next, immunoblotting using two antibodies recognizing IFT-B proteins IFT22 and IFT172 showed that the immune complexes formed by IFT27RNAiRES::YFP and IFT27RNAiRESQ67L::YFP contain both proteins (Figure 15D, left and middle rows).
evidence: This is shown by co-immunoprecipitation data in Figure 15D.

claim: Immunoprecipitation of IFT27RNAiREST19N::YFP failed to bring down IFT22 and IFT172.
source: However, immunoprecipitation of IFT27RNAiREST19N::YFP failed to bring down IFT22 and IFT172 (Figure 15D, right panel).
evidence: This is shown by co-immunoprecipitation data in Figure 15D.

claim: The T19N mutant version of IFT27 is unable to interact with at least two members of the IFT-B complex.
source: In contrast, the T19N mutant version of IFT27 is unable to interact with at least two members of the IFT-B complex.
evidence: This is based on co-immunoprecipitation data showing failure to pull down IFT22 and IFT172.

claim: IFT27 needs to be in a GTP-bound state to interact with the rest of the IFT complex and access the flagellar compartment.
source: Overall, these results demonstrate that IFT27 needs to be in a GTP-bound state to interact with the rest of the IFT complex and access the flagellar compartment.
evidence: This is inferred from the inability of the GDP-locked version to interact with IFT-B proteins and enter the flagellum, while the GTP-locked version can.

claim: IFT27 is a constitutive member of the IFT-B complex in T. brucei.
source: Here, we have shown by immunoprecipitation that IFT27 likely is a constitutive member of the IFT-B complex in T. brucei.
evidence: This is shown by co-immunoprecipitation experiments.

claim: IFT27 performs two separate functions: one in the import of both the IFT-A complex and IFT dynein motors and one in the assembly of the IFT-B complex.
source: These results show that IFT27, an IFT-B protein, performs two separate functions: one in the import of both the IFT-A complex and IFT dynein motors and one in the assembly of the IFT-B complex.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined data showing failure of IFT-A and dynein import in IFT27 RNAi cells, and failure of IFT-B assembly with the GDP-locked mutant.
